full_judgment: 3. The defendant-petitioner appeared in the said suit and filed written statement stating that on the basis of the deed of gift, the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 did not acquire any title and possession in the suit land. She failed to mutate her name in the khatian. He further stated that defendant No. 2, in order to sell the suit land, came to an agreement with the defendant No. 1 on 18-10-1989 and in Insurance of that agreement defendant No. 2 executed and registered a sale deed in favour of the defendant No.1 on 9-8-1993 but inadvertently in the recital of the said deed, the story of bainanama was not mentioned. Accordingly, the defendant No. 2 executed and registered a deed of rectification on 9-12-1993 mentioning the said story of bainanama. The plaintiff’s deed of gift is a forged and fraudulent one. This defendant filed Title Suit No. 115 of 1995 against the plaintiff for his title and for cancellation of that deed of gift dated 30-6-1990. The said suit was re-numbered-as Title Suit No.1 of 2000 and both the suits were taken up for disposal analogously.
